*Note on ¶6:* The phrase "neither water nor …" signals that in the Divine kingdom itself the distinction between truth and its opposite does not arise; all proceeds as one undivided life from the Divine. The missing counterpart in GAP-34 likely names some other natural-plane element (perhaps "fire" = love, or "darkness" = falsity) that likewise has no separate existence there. ---

## Summary of the Spiritual Sense

This passage describes the **interior kingdom of Divine wisdom** — the inmost heaven — before any opposition exists. Everything that dwells there proceeds from the Divine itself: celestial goods (called *gods*), abundances of truth (called *rich ones*), and angelic intelligences (called *angels*). The "five" that recur correspond to the **full complement of spiritual faculties** — perception, acknowledgment, thought, will, and action conjoined into a single living form that receives and reflects the Divine. The mountains, springs, and trees are not landscapes but **elevated states of love, flowing origins of truth, and living perceptions** — all gushing forth from the one Divine source. The "living air" and "living ambrosia" are the **spiritual atmosphere of perception** and the **celestial nourishment of good** that sustain every state within this realm. Nothing here is separate from the Divine; truth and love are not yet distinguished as contraries, because no falsity or self-love has yet arisen to oppose them.

fills.explanation: The subject of the passage is the Father of Greatness, and the clause describes his dwelling within the great land — the Manichaean term for the Divine realm.
The spiritual reading indicates "the inmost degree," and "which is above" specifies the great land of greatness as the highest realm, matching the Kephalaia's spatial language for the Divine heights.
The spiritual reading identifies "the manifest Divine presence," which in Manichaean natural-plane vocabulary is "His face" — the Face of the Father of Greatness, a standard Kephalaia concept.

The spiritual reading says "wisdom and..." — in Manichaean vocabulary "light" corresponds to wisdom, and "His light" denotes the Father's own attribute, consistent with the possessive pattern describing the Father's qualities.

The spiritual reading says "proceeding outward," and in the natural register of the Kephalaia describing the Father's face, "shines out" is the standard expression for light proceeding from the Divine countenance.
The spiritual reading says "the manifest presence of the [Father]," requiring a definite article before "face" — "he has the face of the Father" is the grammatically necessary construction.

The spiritual reading identifies "the manifest presence of the [Divine]" — in Manichaean vocabulary, "the face of the Father" is the standard expression for the visible presence of the Father of Greatness.

The spiritual reading says "the full complement of acknowledgment and worship" — in Manichaean liturgical vocabulary, "five words of praise" is the natural-plane expression for the complete acts of worship directed to the Father.

The text enumerates "living ambrosia" alongside "five elements compound" as coordinate substances that together become an image; "and the" is the natural conjunction linking the celestial nourishment to the five light elements before their compounding.

The spiritual reading says "the complete faculties conjoined into one" — in Manichaean cosmology the five light elements (Ether, Wind, Light, Water, Fire) compound together, and the surrounding references to "living air" and "living ambrosia" confirm these are the light elements.
A connective is needed between "compound" and "they become an image," and the spiritual reading confirms a simple conjunction linking the compounding of the five to their becoming a single form.

The spiritual reading indicates the image and the living air are coordinate realities — "they become an image and the living air... also living" lists them as parallel manifestations of the five compounded elements.
The spiritual reading says "is also animate with the Divine life," requiring the copula "is" to complete "the living air is also living."
The editor's "As" correctly introduces the comparative construction that parallels ¶6's "Just as... so also..." pattern; the spiritual reading confirms the analogical structure.
The spiritual reading indicates emergence from spiritual combats, and "come forth from" is the standard Kephalaia expression for the five light elements emerging from the contests of the greatness.

The spiritual reading says "a perfection of beauty belonging to every capacity of their spiritual form" — in Manichaean vocabulary, "a beautiful form" denotes the restored shape of the light elements after their redemption from contest.
The spiritual reading says "within the kingdom of Divine wisdom," requiring the preposition "in" to form "which exists in the land of light."
The spiritual reading confirms "their life" — the partial word ending in "ife" is completed by "l" to form "life," the standard term for the eternal existence of beings in the Land of Light.

The text enumerates features of the Land of Light — "mountains and springs and trees" — requiring the conjunction "and" to connect the list, paralleling the spiritual reading's enumeration of elevated states, origins, and perceptions.

A relative pronoun is needed to connect "springs and trees" to "gush forth" — the spiritual reading confirms these are origins that "flow forth abundantly," requiring "that" as the relative clause marker.

The preceding clause establishes that everything "came from the Father," and the parallel "so also" construction requires the mountains, springs, and trees to likewise "gush forth from it" — from the same Divine source — matching the spiritual reading's "flow forth abundantly."

The spiritual reading indicates that in the Divine source, truth and love are not separate — "water" corresponds to truth and "fire" to love; "neither water nor fire" expresses their undivided unity in the Land of Light, using two of the five light elements.

The partial word "ar" + "e" completes "are," and the spiritual reading says "these are the realities" — in Kephalaia register, "these are the things which..." is the standard demonstrative construction for summarizing the preceding enumeration.

The chapter's recurring theme of "five" (five elements, five words, five faculties) and the ordinal suffix "-th" combine to form "fifth," indicating this paragraph treats the fifth attribute or element of the Land of Light.

After the ordinal "fifth," the copula and article are needed to introduce the predicate: "The fifth is the great light, the living air" — identifying the fifth element with the great light and the spiritual atmosphere of perception.
